Package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog

Class AamAnnunciationHistoryLog

java.lang.Object
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.HistoryLog
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.AamAnnunciationHistoryLog
public class AamAnnunciationHistoryLog extends HistoryLog
Written when the pump annunciates an active alert, alarm or CGM alert: in the same second as the activation for most ids, then again at multiples of about 5 minutes for as long as the notification stays unacknowledged.

For alerts and alarms, all 1489 records examined (six pumps, Mobi and t:slim X2) follow an AlertActivated / AlarmActivated record with the same category and id on the same pump, and none comes after that notification's AlertAck / AlarmAck. CGM alerts (AamAnnunciationHistoryLog.AamCategory.CGM_ALERT, seen only on the t:slim X2) follow a CGM alert activation with the same id; after an acknowledgement they resume later (60 minutes later for CGM alert 2, then every 5 minutes), consistent with a CGM alert repeat setting. The 2022 t:slim X2 captures contain no records of this type.

The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum do not name this opcode. Bytes 11, 12-13, 18 and 19 are not understood and are exposed raw; bytes 16-17 and 20-25 were zero in all 1680 records examined. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/147.

    • getNotificationId

      public long getNotificationId()
      The id of the notification being annunciated, in the id space of its category: AlertStatusResponse.AlertResponseType for alerts, AlarmStatusResponse.AlarmResponseType for alarms, and the alertId of CgmAlertActivatedDexHistoryLog for CGM alerts. Every id matched the activation record it followed.

      Id 0 is a real alert, LOW_INSULIN_ALERT, not an empty slot: it is frequent because the low-insulin alert is re-annunciated every few minutes until it is acknowledged.

      Returns:
      the alert, alarm or CGM alert id (bytes 14-17)

    • getUnknown11

      public int getUnknown11()
      Byte 11, meaning unknown. Together with getUnknown12() and getUnknown18() it is constant for a given category and id across all 1680 records: 1 for alerts 0, 2, 3, 17, 26 and 54; 2 for alerts 4, 11, 13, 14, 50 and 51; 3 for alarms; 0, 1 or 2 for CGM alerts depending on the id.
      Returns:
      byte 11

      public int getUnknown19()
